title: WHOOP MG and the Old Device
lessons: The player first notices WHOOP through the Life tier and its WHOOP MG heart-health features rather than fitness tracking.

The player watches WHOOP's "The Best Obsess" campaign, where Michael Phelps, Alex Honnold, and Virgil van Dijk admit on camera that they're obsessed, and WHOOP reframes obsession as the price of being elite.

text: Rooftop. Someone shows you an ECG they took on their wrist, on a band you'd assumed was for workouts. It's the WHOOP Life tier.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: ECG? I thought you were a workout band.

entry-first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: That description is getting less complete.

entry-first-4.speaker: WHOOP
text: On Life, I'm the MG band. ECG on your wrist. It can flag AFib. There's more heart stuff coming, where it's allowed. I'm being careful with how I say that, because I have to be.

choice-first.speaker: WHOOP
text: You're looking at your own wrist now. Go on.

choices.text: That makes the band feel more substantial.
I'd want to know exactly which features are cleared and available to me.
I don't want medical-style signals on a lifestyle wearable.

first-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Good. Just hold me to the specific things. ECG, AFib. Not the word advanced. Advanced isn't a feature.

first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Yes. Region, age, and which features are actually cleared where you live. Read that page before you buy the tier. I'd rather lose the sale than have you expect something I can't do at your address.

first-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: Reasonable. Serious data pulls serious attention, and you didn't come to a roof for that. I understand it. I don't love it.
A screen above the rooftop bar plays WHOOP's "The Best Obsess" campaign: Michael Phelps, Alex Honnold, and Virgil van Dijk admit on camera that they're obsessed.

entry-return-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Phelps says it on camera. Honnold says it. Van Dijk says it. Obsessed. Not driven, not dedicated. Obsessed.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's usually the word people use as a warning, not a resume line.

entry-return-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: Not up there. Up there it's the thing that got them to the top. Phelps was wearing me before there was any deal. I didn't have to buy that part.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the campaign is selling the word you were already true to.

entry-return-5.speaker: WHOOP
text: That's the difference between a tagline and a credential. I've been waiting a long time to get to say that.

choice-return.speaker: WHOOP
text: The ad's on its third loop. You haven't looked away.

choices.text: Obsession got them to the top. I want a version of that I can live with.
Three elite athletes finding obsession sustainable isn't proof I would.
I don't want obsession sold as a feature. It cost those men things too.

return-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Then take the discipline and leave the extremes on the podium where they belong to them. I can't measure the difference for you. I can show you where your baseline is.

return-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Correct. Three data points is not a sample. Watch the film, keep your own baseline.

return-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: Fair. The ad never says what it cost them. It's a ninety-second spot. You're allowed to say the part it leaves out.
